data.name: Spirit Whisperer Conversation With Akari
data.detailed_description:
Akari was always online.

Streaming, smiling, playing the part everyone wanted.

Now she’s dead—and still performing for an audience that won’t let her go.

They say it was exhaustion.

They say she collapsed during a livestream.

But they’re wrong.

Tonight, you’ve been contacted not as a fan, but as someone who can speak to the dead.

She’s waiting—cheerful, charming, and hiding something just beneath the surface.

This isn’t just a haunting. It’s her last broadcast.

And you’re the only one tuned in.

Through sharp, emotional conversations, you’ll uncover Akari’s regrets, her fears, and the hidden pain behind the ring lights and emotes.

You’ll choose how to respond—kind or direct, gentle or honest.

You’ll navigate the mask she still wears.

And you’ll guide her toward the one question she’s never asked herself:

What does it mean to be remembered—for who you were, not just how you died?

There will be jokes.

There will be shadows.

There will be moments where her smile doesn’t quite reach her eyes.

This is a visual novel about digital ghosts, broken boundaries, and the price of always performing.

If you’re drawn to bittersweet unravelings, haunted sincerity, and endings that feel a little too personal—this is your stage.

Some ghosts don’t fade.

They just want someone to see them, one last time.

Your answers shape the truth she leaves behind.

There are no easy routes.

Only what she reveals—and what you’re willing to hear.

A story of fame, burnout, and the cost of always being watched.

It all happens in one conversation.

And it might never leave you.

FULL GAME FEATURES:

  • 🎮 10 branching questions that dive into identity, burnout, memory, and regret

  • 📱 9 unique endings shaped by honesty, empathy, and trust

  • 🌟 One expressive sprite: Akari—charming, tragic, and still streaming from the other side

  • 🕯️ A ghost, a whisperer, and the final live that never aired

  • 🕰️ 30–40 minutes to explore all paths—each a different goodbye

"Even in death, she’s still performing for an audience that won’t let go."
